title: The Real Number Line Has No Gaps

steps.body: Between ANY two different numbers on the number line — no matter how close together — there's always another number hiding in between. Rational and irrational numbers are mixed together everywhere on the line; there are no empty patches.

widget.prompt: Between 1.41 and 1.42, is there another number?

choices.label: Yes — for example, 1.415
choices.feedback: Right — decimals can always be extended one more place.

choices.label: No — they're already right next to each other
choices.feedback: They only look adjacent — 1.415 sits exactly between them, and you could keep going even further.

choices.label: Only if it's a whole number
choices.feedback: Whole numbers can't fit between 1.41 and 1.42 at all — but decimals like 1.415 can.

choices.label: Only irrational numbers can fit there
choices.feedback: Both rational (1.415) and irrational numbers can fit in that gap.

steps.body: This matters for locating √2: since 1.4² = 1.96 and 1.5² = 2.25, √2 must be trapped between 1.4 and 1.5. We can keep narrowing forever without ever landing on a clean decimal, because √2 truly never terminates or repeats.
Use the squares to narrow it down.
explanationVariants: 1.96 < 2 < 2.25, and those are exactly 1.4² and 1.5², so √2 is trapped between 1.4 and 1.5.
Since squaring 1.4 undershoots 2 and squaring 1.5 overshoots it, √2 must sit between them.

choices.label: 1.4 and 1.5
choices.feedback: Right — 1.96 < 2 < 2.25 traps √2 right there.

choices.label: 1 and 2
choices.feedback: True, but far less precise than what these specific squares show.

choices.label: 1.96 and 2.25
choices.feedback: Those are the SQUARES, not √2 itself — √2 is between 1.4 and 1.5.

choices.label: 0 and 1
choices.feedback: √2 is bigger than 1, since 1²=1 is less than 2.

steps.body: The number line has no gaps — squaring nearby decimals narrows down any irrational.
takeaways: Between any two numbers, another number always fits.
Squaring two nearby decimals can trap an irrational number between them.
This narrowing technique works for any irrational, to any level of precision.
steps.teaser: Next chapter: using this exact technique to pin down √2, √10, and π on the number line.
